key_insight: MOSS enables autonomous agents to self-evolve by rewriting their own source-level harness (routing, hooks, state invariants) rather than only mutating text artifacts like prompts or skill files, allowing fixes and structural changes after deployment.
problem_solved: Deployed agentic systems remain largely static and rely on human-driven updates; prior self-evolution approaches only alter text-mutable artifacts and cannot fix failures rooted in the agent harness code, leading to recurring faults and brittle behavior.
method: Detect and localize harness-level faults from runtime traces, failure logs, and unit/regression tests.
Synthesize and apply source-level rewrites (program transformations/patches) guided by agent semantics and program synthesis techniques.
Validate changes via automated testing, sandboxed staged deployment, and rollback mechanisms to preserve safety and correctness.
impact: Makes agents continuously maintainable and adaptive post-deployment, reducing manual patch cycles and accelerating fixes for structural/harness bugs while highlighting the need for robust verification and safe deployment practices.

paper_title: MOSS: Self-Evolution through Source-Level Rewriting in Autonomous Agent Systems
paper_authors: Qianshu Cai, Yonggang Zhang, Xianzhang Jia, Wei Xue, Jun Song
